We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three SMILES). Need to choose one that can be further processed through the subsequent templates in order.

We applied 1914389 to one of those (the one with silyl protecting group). It gave two possible outcomes: one precursor (C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO) and a side product (CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC). The side product is likely a protecting group fragment (maybe a silyl group). The route likely expects that after 1914389 we get a molecule that can be processed by 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We applied 1914390 to the first precursor and got a product: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". That seems to be a protected version with silyl group still present.

Then applied 149040 to that, got two fragments: "CC(C)(C)[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F" and "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". So 149040 removes the silyl protecting group and yields a deprotected intermediate.

Now we need to apply 1914391 to that deprotected intermediate to get final precursors (maybe starting materials). Let's try applying 1914391 to "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1".
